title: Change a robot's tool: hold a suction tool on its quick-change flange with one hand while the other locks the ring
instruction: Change the robot's tool to the blue suction-cup tool: with one hand take it from the rack by its handle and hold its plate flat against the robot's tool flange; with the other press the locking ring's lever down until the light on the robot turns green; then let go of both, leaving the tool hanging on the robot, and take both arms back to where they started.
context: Robot cells swap end effectors (grippers, suction cups, welding torches) on quick-change tool changers. When a technician changes a tool by hand, on a manual changer or while recovering a cell after a fault, the new tool has to be held up square against the robot's flange while a locking ring or lever is turned; let go too early and the tool drops, damaging it or the fixture. One hand holds the tool, the other works the lock.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) A robot arm of cast aluminium, fixed (switched off), its base 56 cm forward and 11 cm left of the centre line; its wrist reaches in low, ending in a steel tool flange 6.4 cm across whose face, 2 cm left of the centre line, looks to the right; the flange's axis is 30 cm forward and 8.5 cm above the table. A light on top of the wrist shows red. (2) A steel locking ring 8.8 cm across round the flange, with an orange-painted steel lever reaching 11 cm toward the arms and then bending to the left to a black rubber pad 4.5 by 3 cm (its middle 19 cm forward, 8.3 cm left of the centre line, its top 9.9 cm above the table, with a small lip on its near end). Pressing the pad down turns the ring (up to 35 degrees); the ring stays where it is left. (3) An aluminium tool rack right of the centre line with two slots, each tool lying along the left-right line, its plate facing left toward the flange: a blue suction-cup tool (120 g; a steel plate 6 cm across, its face 30 cm forward and 12 cm right of the centre line; a blue anodised-aluminium body 4.4 cm thick ending in a black nitrile-rubber suction cup 22.5 cm right of the centre line), and the robot's grey aluminium two-finger gripper tool (140 g), the same but 18 cm forward. Each tool has a square steel handle 1.6 cm across on top, 5 cm from its plate's face, its top 14 cm above the table. A tool is seated when its plate's face is within 6 mm of the flange's face, its middle within 1 cm of the flange's axis, its axis within 12 degrees of the flange's and its handle up (within 20 degrees). A tool seated while the ring is within 8 degrees of open is locked on once the ring is turned 25 degrees: it is drawn square onto the flange and the light turns green; turning the ring back below 15 degrees unlocks it. A ring turned with no tool seated locks nothing. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Judged at the end of the trial. 0.0 if the gripper tool was ever locked on. Otherwise 1.0: the suction tool locked on, each gripper's fingertip centre (TCP) at least 4 cm from its handle and from the lever's pad, and both arms back where they started (each TCP within 5 cm of its start); 0.5: the suction tool locked on otherwise; 0.25: the suction tool seated on the flange, with the ring open, at some point; else 0.0. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s with the suction tool still.
reset_notes: Turn the ring back open, take the suction tool off and lay both tools back in the rack.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control). Simplified: the robot is fixed, and its flange has no bayonet lugs or locating pins; the lock is a fixed joint the task file switches on when the ring turns 25 degrees with a tool seated. The ring is a hinge with a spring that the task file moves to hold it where it is left. Cameras 1280 x 704 (Dream-1 sees 320 x 176).
